hero.title: Sources of Information of Pre-History
hero.description: Explore the archaeological, literary, foreign accounts, and scientific dating methods that reconstruct India's prehistoric past — essential for UPSC Prelims & Mains.

timeline.title: Evolution of Source Studies
timeline.description: Click on any source card below to view its key archaeological characteristics, dating methods, and historical utility.

cards.details:
Excavations — Systematic digging of ancient sites to uncover material remains: tools, pottery, structures, burials. Key excavations: Bhimbetka (V. S. Wakankar), Inamgaon (H. D. Sankalia), Mehrgarh (J. F. Jarrige), Attirampakkam (Shanti Pappu).

Inscriptions (Epigraphy) — Writings on stone, metal, pottery. For prehistoric context, Ashokan edicts (3rd cent. BCE) are the earliest decipherable inscriptions in India. Prehistoric rock paintings & graffiti at Bhimbetka provide symbolic evidence.

Coins (Numismatics) — Punch-marked coins (c. 6th cent. BCE onward) provide economic & political information for proto-historic & early historic periods.

Monuments & Megaliths — Dolmens, menhirs, stone circles (South Indian Iron Age) — burial markers that indicate social hierarchy and belief systems.

cards.date: Vedas, Epics, Puranas, Buddhist & Jain Texts
cards.details:
Vedas — Rigveda (oldest, c. 1500-1200 BCE) provides earliest literary glimpse of Vedic society: pastoralism, tribal polity, river-based geography (Sapta Sindhu).

Brahmanas & Aranyakas — Ritual texts describing sacrificial practices, social hierarchy, and geographical expansion.

Upanishads — Philosophical treatises (c. 800-500 BCE) reflecting late Vedic intellectual ferment.

Epics — Ramayana & Mahabharata (core composed c. 500-400 BCE) — contain geographical, political, and cultural descriptions of Iron Age India.

Puranas — Genealogies of kings, cosmological accounts, historical traditions.

Buddhist & Jain Texts — Tripitakas (Pali canon), Jatakas, Angas — provide urban, social, and economic data for 6th cent. BCE onward.

Greek & Roman:
• Herodotus (5th cent. BCE) — 'Father of History' — mentions India as 'Indica'
• Megasthenes (c. 300 BCE) — Indica — detailed account of Mauryan administration, society, geography (only fragments survive)
• Pliny the Elder (1st cent. CE) — Natural History — India-Rome trade
• Ptolemy (2nd cent. CE) — Geography & map of India
• Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (1st cent. CE) — trade routes, ports, exports

Chinese:
• Fa-Hien (5th cent. CE) — Gupta period, Buddhist pilgrimage
• Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) (7th cent. CE) — Harsha's India, Nalanda University
• I-Tsing (7th cent. CE) — Buddhist monastic life

Persian:
• Al-Biruni (11th cent. CE) — Kitab-ul-Hind — Indian society, science, religion

Radiocarbon (¹⁴C) Dating — Most common method for organic remains up to ~50,000 years. Measures decay of carbon-14. Key for Neolithic & Chalcolithic sites.

Dendrochronology — Tree-ring dating. Useful for wooden artifacts & climate reconstruction. Limited in India.

Thermoluminescence (TL) — Dates pottery & burnt clay (last heating event). Useful for Harappan & Chalcolithic pottery.

Potassium-Argon (K-Ar) — Dates volcanic rock. Used for earliest hominin sites (e.g., Olduvai Gorge).

Uranium-Series — Dates cave deposits, coral, and carbonate. Used for Bhimbetka & other rock shelter sites.

Optically Stimulated Luminescence (OSL) — Dates sediment burial. Used for Attirampakkam (1.5 MYA).

Stratigraphy — Relative dating based on layer sequence. Seriation — relative dating by artifact typology.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Palace Hooks
mnemonics.description: Use these memory cues to quickly memorize key scholars, scripts, and travellers for the UPSC exam.

items.title: Mnemonic 1: Earliest Prehistoric Discovery
items.decryption: Robert Bruce **Foote** (Father of Indian Prehistory) **Found** the first Paleolithic tool (handaxe) at **Pallavaram** (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) in 1863.

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Brahmi Decipherment
items.decryption: **James Prinsep** deciphered the **Brahmi** script in 1837, unlocking the earliest written records of Ashoka.

items.title: Mnemonic 3: Chronology of Key Chinese Travellers
items.decryption: Chronological order of arrival in India: **Fa-Hien** (4th-5th cent. CE) → **Hiuen Tsang** (Xuanzang, 7th cent. CE) → **I-Tsing** (7th cent. CE).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Trap 1: Earliest Written Records vs. Deciphered script: While Harappan seals contain the earliest written records in India, they remain undeciphered. The **Ashokan edicts** written in Brahmi script are the earliest deciphered written records.

Trap 2: Absolute vs. Relative Dating: Stratigraphy and seriation are **relative** dating methods (which establish chronological sequence relative to other items). Radiocarbon, TL, OSL, and Potassium-Argon are **absolute** methods (which yield calendar age ranges).

Trap 3: Megasthenes' Indica survival: Megasthenes' Indica does not exist in its original copy. We only know its contents through fragments cited in later works of Greek and Roman writers like Arrian, Strabo, Diodorus, and Pliny.

sections.title: 1. Archaeological Excavations & Major Sites
sections.content:
Prehistory, by definition, lacks written records, making archaeological excavations the primary source of information. Archaeologists use material remains like stone tools, pottery, organic materials, and architectural remnants to reconstruct past lifeways. Key methodologies and sites include:

Excavation Methods
  • Grid Method: Introduced by Mortimer Wheeler, utilizing square trenches with 'baulks' (unexcavated walls of earth) to maintain vertical control and capture stratigraphy.
  • Vertical vs. Horizontal: Vertical excavation acts as a chronological probe (cutting deep into layers to establish timeline), while horizontal excavation exposes structural layouts across a broad area.
Key Prehistoric Excavations
  • Attirampakkam (TN): Excavated by Shanti Pappu; established the oldest Acheulian tool workshop in India, dated to c. 1.5 MYA.
  • Bhimbetka (MP): Discovered by V.S. Wakankar (1957); continuous occupation sequence (Paleolithic to Medieval) shown across 700+ shelters.
  • Mehrgarh (Balochistan): J.F. Jarrige (1974); earliest Neolithic village in South Asia (c. 7000 BCE).

masteryZone.q: Who introduced the systematic grid method of excavation in India to maintain stratigraphical control?
masteryZone.sol: Mortimer Wheeler introduced the grid method of excavation, which used unexcavated 'baulks' between square trenches to preserve vertical stratigraphy.

masteryZone.q: In which year were the famous prehistoric rock shelters of Bhimbetka discovered by Dr. V.S. Wakankar?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. V.S. Wakankar discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters in 1957 while traveling by train and noticing the sandstone rock formations.

masteryZone.q: Which archaeological site has yielded the earliest evidence of a Neolithic village settlement in South Asia?
masteryZone.sol: Mehrgarh in Balochistan, Pakistan, represents the earliest Neolithic village in South Asia, dating back to c. 7000 BCE.

masteryZone.q: The Lower Paleolithic site of Attirampakkam, which established a 1.5-million-year-old Acheulian history, is located near which city?
masteryZone.sol: Attirampakkam is located in the Kortallayar River basin near Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Excavated by Shanti Pappu, it is dated to c. 1.5 MYA.

masteryZone.q: The major Chalcolithic site of Inamgaon, which features a fortified settlement and mud houses, is located on which river?
masteryZone.sol: Inamgaon is a large Chalcolithic settlement of the Jorwe culture located on the banks of the Ghod River, a tributary of the Bhima River in Maharashtra.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites are classified as Paleolithic in the Indian subcontinent? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Attirampakkam, Hunsgi, and Bhimbetka are Paleolithic sites, while Mehrgarh is a Neolithic site.

masteryZone.q: Which excavations were directed or co-directed by French archaeologist Jean-François Jarrige? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Jean-François Jarrige directed the excavations at Mehrgarh, Nausharo, and Pirak in Balochistan. Attirampakkam was excavated by Shanti Pappu.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following features are characteristic of horizontal excavations? (Select all that apply)
opts: Exposes structural layouts of a single period
Acts as a quick chronological probe
masteryZone.sol: Horizontal excavations expose wide spatial layouts of a single period to understand settlement patterns. Vertical excavations serve as chronological probes.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites represent the Mesolithic phase in India? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bagor, Adamgarh, and Langhnaj are famous Mesolithic sites. Inamgaon is a Chalcolithic settlement.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following elements did Mortimer Wheeler introduce to Indian archaeology? (Select all that apply)
opts: Focus on the Harappan citadel layouts
masteryZone.sol: Mortimer Wheeler introduced the grid system, structured training at Taxila, and focused on Harappan citadel fortifications. C-14 was introduced in India after his tenure.

masteryZone.q: Vertical excavation is primarily designed to establish a detailed site timeline rather than uncover structural layouts.
masteryZone.sol: Vertical excavation cuts deep through layers to serve as a chronological probe to build a historical sequence.

masteryZone.q: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the first Indian Paleolithic tool at Bhimbetka in 1863.
masteryZone.sol: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the first Paleolithic tool (a handaxe) at Pallavaram near Chennai, not Bhimbetka.

masteryZone.q: The archaeological site of Hunsgi utilized limestone instead of quartzite for tool manufacture.
masteryZone.sol: The Hunsgi-Baichbal valley is unique because Lower Paleolithic hominins utilized locally available limestone for their Acheulian tools.

masteryZone.q: The grid method leaves unexcavated earth walls called 'baulks' to show soil stratigraphy.
masteryZone.sol: Baulks are vertical dirt walls left between grids to allow continuous recording and observation of soil layers.

masteryZone.q: Lahuradewa is located in the Indus valley and is known for early wheat cultivation.
masteryZone.sol: Lahuradewa is located in Sant Kabir Nagar, Uttar Pradesh (Ganga Valley), and is famous for early domestic rice evidence, not Indus valley wheat.

masteryZone.q: Stratigraphy is based on the principle that the lowest layer of undisturbed soil is the oldest.
masteryZone.sol: The Law of Superposition states that in an undisturbed stratigraphic sequence, the oldest layers lie at the bottom.

masteryZone.q: All Chalcolithic cultures in India are contemporary with the early Harappan civilization.
masteryZone.sol: Most Chalcolithic cultures (like Jorwe, Malwa, Banas) were post-Harappan or late Harappan rural farming communities existing after 2000 BCE.

masteryZone.q: Dr. Shanti Pappu's excavations at Attirampakkam pushed the history of Indian Acheulian tools back to c. 1.5 million years ago.
masteryZone.sol: Excavations by the Sharma Centre for Heritage Education, led by Shanti Pappu, established a date of c. 1.5 MYA using cosmogenic nuclide burial dating.

masteryZone.q: The first Paleolithic tool in India was discovered by Robert Bruce Foote at ________ in 1863.
masteryZone.sol: Robert Bruce Foote discovered a handaxe at Pallavaram near Madras on May 30, 1863.

masteryZone.q: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are situated in the Vindhyan range of the state of ________.
masteryZone.sol: Bhimbetka rock shelters are situated in the Raisen District of Madhya Pradesh.

masteryZone.q: The excavation method that exposes large horizontal layouts of settlements is known as ________ excavation.
masteryZone.sol: Horizontal (or area) excavations are used to expose the spatial structure of a site during a single occupational phase.

masteryZone.q: The earliest Neolithic village in South Asia, Mehrgarh, is situated in the modern province of ________.
masteryZone.sol: Mehrgarh is located in Balochistan, Pakistan, near the Bolan Pass.

masteryZone.q: The excavator of the crucial Neolithic site of Mehrgarh was French archaeologist ________.
masteryZone.sol: Jean-François Jarrige excavated Mehrgarh from 1974 to 1986.

masteryZone.q: The Lower Paleolithic workshops in the Hunsgi-Baichbal valley are located in the state of ________.
masteryZone.sol: Hunsgi is located in the Yadgir district of Karnataka.

masteryZone.q: The unexcavated walls of earth left between grid trenches to monitor layers are called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Baulks are narrow vertical partitions of soil left between excavation squares.

masteryZone.q: The site of Koldihwa, which yielded early corded pottery and rice husks, is located in the ________ river valley.
masteryZone.sol: Koldihwa is located in the Belan river valley in Uttar Pradesh.

masteryZone.q: Match the prehistoric excavations with their lead scholars:
masteryZone.sol: Bhimbetka was discovered by V.S. Wakankar; Attirampakkam was excavated by Shanti Pappu; Mehrgarh was excavated by Jean-François Jarrige.

masteryZone.q: Match the prehistoric site with its key geographic river basin:
masteryZone.sol: Inamgaon is on the Ghod, Koldihwa is in the Belan valley, and Bagor is on the Kothari River.

masteryZone.q: Match the excavation methodology term with its description:
masteryZone.sol: Baulks are soil walls showing stratigraphy, vertical excavation is a chronological probe, and horizontal excavation exposes spatial layouts.

masteryZone.q: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Prehistory'?
masteryZone.sol: Robert Bruce Foote, a British geologist who discovered the first Paleolithic handaxe in 1863.

masteryZone.q: Which excavation method is preferred to understand the horizontal layout and spatial planning of a prehistoric village?
masteryZone.sol: Horizontal (or area) excavation method.

masteryZone.q: Name the site that has yielded the earliest evidence of agricultural domestication in the Ganga Valley.
masteryZone.sol: Lahuradewa, located in Sant Kabir Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.

masteryZone.q: Why are the rock shelters of Bhimbetka globally significant?
masteryZone.sol: They preserve a continuous sequence of rock art paintings spanning from the Upper Paleolithic to the Medieval period.

masteryZone.q: What raw stone material was primarily used by Paleolithic toolmakers at Hunsgi?
masteryZone.sol: Limestone, which was locally abundant in the Hunsgi-Baichbal valley.

masteryZone.q: Which major site in Maharashtra belongs to the post-Harappan Jorwe Chalcolithic culture?
masteryZone.sol: Inamgaon (or Daimabad).

masteryZone.q: What is the function of a 'baulk' in archaeological grid excavations?
masteryZone.sol: It acts as a physical wall showing the vertical stratigraphy and soil layers of the site.

masteryZone.q: Which Paleolithic excavation in India has been dated to c. 1.5 million years ago using cosmogenic nuclides?
masteryZone.sol: Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Vertical excavations are referred to as chronological probes.
Reason (R): They cut deep into occupational layers to reveal historical sequences and timelines rather than wide spatial structures.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Vertical excavations cut deep through levels specifically to build a chronology.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Soan Valley represents a purely handaxe-dominated Acheulian culture.
Reason (R): River terraces in the northwest yielded Pebble tools (choppers) distinct from the southern bifacial traditions.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false but R is true. The Soan valley is characterized by Soanian pebble-chopper tool traditions, not handaxe-dominated Acheulian (though some overlap occurs).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Bhimbetka shelters were selected for continuous occupation from the Paleolithic to Medieval times.
Reason (R): The site offered natural sandstones, permanent water sources, and abundant forest resources.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains why early humans continuously inhabited Bhimbetka.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Mehrgarh is known as the breadbasket of early Balochistan.
Reason (R): It has yielded the earliest evidence of cultivated wheat and barley alongside domesticated sheep and goats in South Asia.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why it is called the breadbasket.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Shanti Pappu's excavations at Attirampakkam utilized vertical grid methodology.
Reason (R): Grid excavations allow precise vertical mapping of soil layers and artifact positioning.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true but R is not the direct, unique explanation of A (it defines grid excavation generally).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Lower Paleolithic humans are often called 'Quartzite Men' in India.
Reason (R): Quartzite was the exclusive material used throughout the Mesolithic and Neolithic periods.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true but R is false. Mesolithic and Neolithic tools utilized chert, chalcedony, and polished stones, not crude quartzite.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The grid method of excavation is highly superior to trial trenches.
Reason (R): It maintains unexcavated baulks that serve as permanent stratigraphical references.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains the superiority of the grid method.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Lahuradewa has disputed Mehrgarh's status as the sole earliest agricultural origin point in South Asia.
Reason (R): Domesticated rice grains at Lahuradewa date back to c. 9000-8000 BCE, indicating independent development in the Ganga basin.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains why Lahuradewa challenged Mehrgarh's primacy.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Bhimbetka:
1. It was discovered by Dr. V.S. Wakankar in 1957.
2. It has yielded uninterrupted cultural deposits from the Lower Paleolithic to the historic period.
3. It is situated on the Vindhyan range in Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: All three statements are correct. Bhimbetka exhibits long-term continuous human occupation and stratigraphy.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding excavation methodologies:
1. Vertical excavations expose a broad spatial layout of buildings.
2. Horizontal excavations act as deep chronological probes.
3. The grid method was introduced in India by Mortimer Wheeler.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Only statement 3 is correct. Vertical excavations are chronological probes, and horizontal excavations expose broad layouts.

masteryZone.q:
Regarding the site of Mehrgarh, which of the following statements are correct?
1. It is a Neolithic site located near the Bolan Pass.
2. It has yielded the earliest evidence of pottery in South Asia prior to farming.
3. Excavations show a transition from mud brick shelters to circular huts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Only statement 1 is correct. Mehrgarh did not yield pottery *prior* to farming (pottery appeared in Phase II, after farming started). shelter transition was from circular/irregular to rectangular mud-brick structures.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Attirampakkam:
1. It has yielded evidence of Acheulian tool technology.
2. It was excavated extensively by Robert Bruce Foote in 1863.
3. The antiquity of the site has been dated using cosmogenic nuclide burial dating.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. While Foote discovered tools near Madras in 1863, Attirampakkam's modern excavations establishing the 1.5 MYA date were directed by Shanti Pappu.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the site of Inamgaon, consider the following statements:
1. It is a large Chalcolithic settlement belonging to the Malwa culture.
2. It has yielded evidence of a fortified wall and moat.
3. Specialized burials of children in jars have been excavated here.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Inamgaon belongs primarily to the Jorwe culture (c. 1400-700 BCE), not the Malwa culture.

masteryZone.q: Why are unexcavated dirt walls (baulks) left between grid trenches during archaeological excavations?
masteryZone.sol: Baulks are left as vertical dirt walls between grids to show the stratigraphy (soil layers) of the site. They allow archaeologists to draw and monitor cross-sections of soil profiles to understand the depositional history and sequence of layers.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Hathnora fossil (found in Madhya Pradesh) crucial to the study of early humans in India?
masteryZone.sol: Hathnora yielded a skull cap (Homo erectus narmadensis) which represents the first and only human fossil of the Middle Pleistocene epoch found in the entire Indian subcontinent, confirming early hominin presence parallel to Neanderthals or Denisovans.

masteryZone.q: Why is Lahuradewa considered a revolutionary excavation for South Asian agricultural history?
masteryZone.sol: Lahuradewa pushed back the antiquity of agriculture in South Asia to c. 9000-8000 BCE by yielding domesticated rice grains. It proved that agricultural origins were not restricted to Mehrgarh (wheat/barley) but developed independently in the Ganga valley.

masteryZone.q: How does vertical excavation differ from horizontal excavation in its archaeological objective?
masteryZone.sol: Vertical excavation cuts deep down in a narrow area to establish a chronological sequence of cultures (stratigraphic probe). Horizontal excavation clears a wide area of a single phase to expose structural layouts, trade patterns, and town planning.

masteryZone.q: How did archaeologists date the Acheulian tools at Attirampakkam when organic remains were absent?
masteryZone.sol: Archaeologists used cosmogenic nuclide burial dating on the soil/sediment layers containing the stone tools. This method measures the decay of radioactive isotopes (like Beryllium-10 and Aluminum-26) in quartz grains since they were buried.

masteryZone.q: How does the site of Hunsgi illustrate Lower Paleolithic spatial organization?
masteryZone.sol: Hunsgi features distinct concentrations of limestone artifacts, tools, and debitage scattered across a valley. This shows a settlement-subsistence pattern where hominins used tool factory/workshop sites alongside springs for manufacturing, returning repeatedly.

masteryZone.q: An archaeologist finds a site with stratified layers: Layer 1 (top) has iron sickles and black-and-red pottery; Layer 2 has tiny geometric blades (microliths) with no metals; Layer 3 has crude handaxes. Reconstruct the chronological transition of this site.
masteryZone.sol: This site represents a classic evolutionary sequence of prehistory and protohistory: Layer 3 represents the Paleolithic period (crude handaxes), Layer 2 represents a transition to the Mesolithic period (microliths), and Layer 1 represents the transition to the Iron Age (iron sickles and specialized pottery).

masteryZone.q: During excavations in a valley, a team uncovers an area filled with stone chips and half-finished tools, but no domestic pottery, hearths, or animal bones. Reconstruct the function of this site.
masteryZone.sol: The absence of hearths, bones, and domestic wares combined with massive debitage (chips) and unfinished tools indicates this was a specialized factory or workshop site. Hominins came here to exploit local stone resources to manufacture tools and carried finished tools to their habitation areas.

masteryZone.q: At a river basin site, early layers show animal bones that are 80% wild species (deer, rhinos). Later strata show bones that are 70% domestic species (cattle, sheep). Reconstruct the socio-economic change that occurred.
masteryZone.sol: This sequence reflects a clear transition from a hunter-gatherer economy (dependent on wild game) to a pastoralist/domesticated economy (animal husbandry). This represents the transitional Mesolithic phase or early Neolithic revolution where animal taming replaced wild hunting.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of stratigraphic superposition to a beginner. Use a common daily-life analogy.
masteryZone.sol: Stratigraphic superposition is the rule that older things lie at the bottom, and newer things lie on top. A great analogy is a laundry basket: the clothes you wore on Monday are at the absolute bottom, while the clothes you wore on Friday are on the top. Similarly, in soil, older historical layers are buried deepest, while newer layers sit closest to the surface.

masteryZone.q: How would you explain the difference between vertical and horizontal excavations? Create a mnemonic or visual trick.
masteryZone.sol: Think of a cake: Vertical excavation is like cutting a single, deep slice of cake to see all the colorful layers inside (the chronological timeline). Horizontal excavation is like peeling off the entire top layer of frosting to see the design spread across the cake (the settlement layout). Vertical is a 'Time Probe', Horizontal is a 'Space Map'.

masteryZone.q: Explain why Mehrgarh is called the 'cradle of agriculture' in the Indian subcontinent.
masteryZone.sol: Mehrgarh is called the cradle of agriculture because it shows the transition from hunting-gathering to settled farming (c. 7000 BCE). It is the earliest site in South Asia with mud-brick granaries, domesticated sheep/goats, and cultivated barley/wheat, marking the dawn of the Neolithic revolution in the subcontinent.

sections.title: 2. Epigraphy (Inscriptions) & Numismatics (Coins)
sections.content:
While inscriptions and coins represent historical sources, they provide crucial anchor points for prehistoric transitions, chronology, and early state formation in protohistory.

Epigraphy & Inscriptions
  • Epigraphy: The study of writings engraved on stone, metal plates, wood, or pottery.
  • Earliest Deciphered: Ashokan Edicts (3rd Century BCE), written in Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts, deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.
  • Symbolic Antecedents: Prehistoric rock art (Bhimbetka), undeciphered Harappan seals, and Megalithic post-firing graffiti represent pre-writing stages of information storage.
Numismatics & Coins
  • Numismatics: The study of coins, which sheds light on trade routes, metal purity, artistic trends, and political boundaries.
  • Punch-Marked Coins: Earliest Indian coins (c. 6th century BCE), minted in silver and copper, bearing symbols of sun, hills, trees, and animals.
  • Foreign Dynamics: Indo-Greeks introduced die-struck coins with ruler portraits and bilingual legends; Guptas represented the golden era of numismatics with gold coins ('dinars').

masteryZone.q: The study of inscriptions is known as ________, while the study of historical handwriting style is called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Epigraphy is the study of inscriptions. Palaeography is the study of ancient writing styles and handwriting scripts.

masteryZone.q: Which British scholar deciphered the Brahmi script on Ashokan inscriptions in the year 1837?
masteryZone.sol: James Prinsep, the founding editor of the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, deciphered Brahmi in 1837.

masteryZone.q: Which is the earliest copper-plate inscription in India that mentions famine relief measures, believed to be Mauryan?
masteryZone.sol: The Sohgaura copper plate (Gorakhpur, UP) is the earliest known copper plate in India, written in Brahmi, detailing state storehouse famine distribution.

masteryZone.q: Which dynasty introduced the first gold coins in India with portraits of kings and bilingual legends?
masteryZone.sol: Indo-Greek rulers (c. 2nd century BCE) were the first to issue coins with portraits and bilingual (Greek/Kharoshthi) legends in India.

masteryZone.q: The study of coins, which includes their composition, weight standards, and minting techniques, is called:
masteryZone.sol: Numismatics is the scientific study of coins, tokens, paper money, and related objects.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following scripts were used in the inscriptions of Ashoka? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Ashokan inscriptions used Brahmi (major), Kharoshthi (northwest), Aramaic, and Greek scripts.

masteryZone.q: Which metals were primarily used to manufacture the earliest Punch-Marked Coins (c. 6th cent. BCE)? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The earliest punch-marked coins (c. 6th century BCE) were minted in silver and copper. Gold coins appeared much later.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following descriptions accurately characterize Kharoshthi script? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Kharoshthi script is written right to left, used in the northwest under Aramaic influence, and deciphered primarily by James Prinsep, Lassen, and Norris in the 1830s.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following inscriptions contain records of the Saka ruler Rudradaman I? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Rudradaman I's famous Sanskrit inscription is located on the rock at Junagadh (Gujarat).

masteryZone.q: Which elements can be analyzed using Numismatics to reconstruct historical realities? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Coins indicate economy, territory, and metallurgy. They represent written scripts but do not directly record spoken languages.

masteryZone.q: The Kharoshthi script was written from left to right, similar to Brahmi.
masteryZone.sol: Kharoshthi was written from right to left, while Brahmi was written from left to right.

masteryZone.q: Punch-marked coins bear legends of kings detailing their dates of coronation.
masteryZone.sol: Punch-marked coins contain only symbols (hills, tree, sun) punched onto metal blanks; they do not contain written legends of kings.

masteryZone.q: The earliest deciphered inscriptions in India are written in the Brahmi script.
masteryZone.sol: The Ashokan edicts (3rd century BCE) in Brahmi are the earliest deciphered written records in India.

masteryZone.q: Palaeography is the science of reconstructing ancient languages from written inscriptions.
masteryZone.sol: Palaeography is the study of ancient writing styles and evolution of scripts, not languages.

masteryZone.q: The Sohgaura copper plate inscription is written in Prakrit and Brahmi script.
masteryZone.sol: The Sohgaura plate is written in the Prakrit language using Ashokan Brahmi characters.

masteryZone.q: Indian gold coins were minted in the largest quantities during the Gupta Empire.
masteryZone.sol: Guptas issued the largest number of gold coins (known as dinars), depicting rich artistic variants, though Kushanas issued gold coins with higher purity.

masteryZone.q: Punch-marked coins were manufactured by casting molten metal in pre-designed clay molds.
masteryZone.sol: Punch-marked coins were made by cutting metal sheets into shapes and then punching symbols onto them, not by casting in molds.

masteryZone.q: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script while serving as an officer in the Mint of Calcutta.
masteryZone.sol: James Prinsep was an assay master in the Calcutta Mint, which gave him deep experience in coin metals and scripts.

masteryZone.q: The science of studying inscriptions engraved on stone, clay, or copper is called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Epigraphy is the branch of science dedicated to deciphering and reading inscriptions.

masteryZone.q: The Brahmi script on Ashokan edicts was deciphered in the year ________.
masteryZone.sol: James Prinsep successfully deciphered the script in 1837.

masteryZone.q: The earliest coins of India, which lacked inscriptions and had only symbols, are called ________ coins.
masteryZone.sol: These are called punch-marked coins (or Aahat coins in Hindi) due to symbols being punched individually onto sheets.

masteryZone.q: The famous Junagadh Rock Inscription of Rudradaman I is the first major inscription written in ________ language.
masteryZone.sol: The Junagadh inscription (c. 150 CE) is the first major long inscription written in classical Sanskrit.

masteryZone.q: Gupta gold coins are officially designated in contemporary inscriptions as ________.
masteryZone.sol: Contemporary Gupta inscriptions refer to gold coins as 'dinars', derived from the Roman denarius.

masteryZone.q: The ancient writing style found in northwestern Ashokan edicts, written from right to left, is ________.
masteryZone.sol: Kharoshthi script was used primarily in the Gandhara region.

masteryZone.q: The study of seals and clay stampings used to authenticate ancient trade packages is called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Sigillography (or sphragistics) is the study of wax, clay, or lead seals.

masteryZone.q: The earliest written records of India, still undeciphered, belong to the ________ Civilization.
masteryZone.sol: Harappan pictographic seals represent the earliest writing in South Asia but remain undeciphered.

masteryZone.q: Match the ancient inscriptions with their associated rulers:
masteryZone.sol: Allahabad Prasasti belongs to Samudragupta; Junagadh is of Rudradaman I; Aihole belongs to Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II.

masteryZone.q: Match the script with its writing direction:
masteryZone.sol: Brahmi is left to right, Kharoshthi is right to left, and Boustrophedon alternates directions.

masteryZone.q: Match the coin type with its historical significance:

options.text: Minted largest numbers of gold coins

masteryZone.sol: Punch-marked coins are the earliest currency, Indo-Greeks introduced portraits, and Guptas minted the largest number of gold coins.

masteryZone.q: What is the term for the study of seals and sealings?
masteryZone.sol: Sigillography (or Sphragistics).

masteryZone.q: Which script did James Prinsep decipher to read Mauryan records in 1837?
masteryZone.sol: Brahmi script.

masteryZone.q: Why are punch-marked coins called 'punch-marked'?
masteryZone.sol: Because symbols were punched individually onto ready-cut sheets of metal, rather than cast from molds.

masteryZone.q: What language was used in the earliest deciphered inscriptions of India?
masteryZone.sol: Prakrit language (written in Brahmi script).

masteryZone.q: Which Gupta ruler is depicted on coins playing the lute (veena)?
masteryZone.sol: Samudragupta.

masteryZone.q: Name the oldest deciphered Sanskrit inscription found in western India.
masteryZone.sol: Junagadh Rock Inscription of Rudradaman I (c. 150 CE).

masteryZone.q: Why did the Indo-Greeks coin system represent a major technological advance over punch-marked coins?
masteryZone.sol: They introduced die-striking methods that allowed portraiture and bilingual legends, rather than irregular stamps.

masteryZone.q: Which script was written from right to left under Aramaic influence in the northwestern edicts of Ashoka?
masteryZone.sol: Kharoshthi script.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Mauryan punch-marked coins are dated based on stratigraphic layer association rather than inscriptions.
Reason (R): They do not contain any written legends, king names, or date markings.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains why stratigraphic dating is required for punch-marked coins.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Classical Sanskrit emerged as the primary epigraphical language of royal orders starting in the 3rd century BCE.
Reason (R): The earliest inscriptions, like the edicts of Ashoka, were written exclusively in Sanskrit.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false but R is false. Ashokan inscriptions were written in Prakrit (using Brahmi/Kharoshthi), not Sanskrit. Classical Sanskrit emerged later in inscriptions around 150 CE.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Indo-Greek coinages are highly valued for reconstructing historical chronologies.
Reason (R): They introduced die-struck portraits of kings, helping researchers identify reigns and genealogical orders.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explain how Indo-Greek coins assist in establishing chronology.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Guptas issued coins with high artistic quality but varying gold purity.
Reason (R): Gold coins served as dynastic symbols and ritual currency rather than standard daily-life commercial exchange tokens.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true but R is not the direct cause of varying purity (which was linked to late Gupta economic decline and Roman trade shift).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Kharoshthi script was deciphered through bilingual coins.
Reason (R): Indo-Greek coins bore names in both Greek and Kharoshthi characters, allowing scholars to translate the symbols.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains the exact mechanism of Kharoshthi's decipherment.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Numismatics is a secondary source for political history but primary for economic history.
Reason (R): Coins reveal metal purity, minting volumes, and trade networks directly reflecting fiscal state capacity.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains why coins represent primary sources for economic histories.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Inscriptions are considered more reliable than literary sources.
Reason (R): They are generally engraved on permanent materials, making them less prone to interpolation and copyist errors over centuries.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Mauryan state authority exercised monopolistic control over coin minting.
Reason (R): Inscriptions like Ashokan Edicts detail the punishments for individuals caught fabricating local punch-marked coins.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true but R is false. While the Arthashastra lists metal regulations, Ashokan Edicts do not contain any references to coins, minting, or coin counterfeiting punishments.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the decipherment of ancient Indian scripts:
1. James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837.
2. In Mauryan inscriptions, Brahmi script was written from right to left.
3. The earliest bilingual coins that helped decipher Kharoshthi script were issued by Kushana rulers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Only statement 1 is correct. Brahmi was written left to right. Bilingual coins utilized for Kharoshthi decipherment were Indo-Greek, not Kushan.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding ancient Indian coinages:
1. Punch-marked coins lack any dates or names of kings.
2. Indo-Greeks introduced bilingual gold coins depicting portraitures.
3. Kushanas were the first dynasty in India to issue gold coins in large quantities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: All three statements are correct. Kushanas standardized gold coinage in India following Indo-Greek styles.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to Ashokan Edicts, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Most edicts in the Gangetic plains are written in Prakrit and Brahmi script.
2. Northwestern edicts near Kandahar are written in Greek and Aramaic.
3. Kharoshthi script was used exclusively in his eastern Indian edicts.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Kharoshthi was used exclusively in northwestern edicts (like Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra), not eastern India.

masteryZone.q:
Regarding epigraphical history, consider the following statements:
1. The Sohgaura copper plate is the earliest deciphered copper plate in India.
2. The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I represents the first long Sanskrit inscription.
3. Allahabad Prasasti of Samudragupta was composed in Prakrit by Harishena.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Allahabad Prasasti was composed in classical Sanskrit using Champu kavya style by Harishena, not Prakrit.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the study of coins (Numismatics):
1. The presence of Roman gold coins in South India indicates a high trade surplus in favor of India.
2. A decline in gold purity during late Gupta reigns is interpreted as a sign of economic crisis.
3. The symbols on punch-marked coins have been fully deciphered as representing the names of Maurya ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The symbols on punch-marked coins are not deciphered as minister names; they remain symbolic representations.

masteryZone.q: Why are inscriptions considered more reliable historical sources than literary texts?
masteryZone.sol: Inscriptions are engraved on stone or metal, making them durable and highly resistant to changes over time. Unlike literary texts, which were manually copied over generations (introducing errors, additions, and interpolations), inscriptions remain original, unaltered documents of their specific period.

masteryZone.q: Why did the discovery of bilingual coins in Afghanistan and northwest India solve the mystery of the Kharoshthi script?
masteryZone.sol: Scholars like James Prinsep could read the Greek legends on one side of Indo-Greek coins, which contained known royal names. By comparing these known Greek names with the unknown Kharoshthi characters on the reverse side, they matched sounds to symbols, unlocking the key to reading Kharoshthi.

masteryZone.q: Why does a sudden change in coin metals or purity at a site indicate economic shifts?
masteryZone.sol: Coins reflect the fiscal strength of a state. A shift from pure gold to alloyed gold or copper, or a decrease in coin size and volume, shows that the treasury was facing deficits, trade networks were declining, or raw metal access was lost, reflecting economic distress.

masteryZone.q: How does the study of coins (Numismatics) help archaeologists map the territorial boundaries of ancient dynasties?
masteryZone.sol: The spatial distribution of coin hoards indicates a dynasty's political control or trade domain. While a single stray coin could represent trade, finding multiple clusters and hoards of a specific dynasty's currency in a geographic region strongly suggests administrative control and taxation over that area.

masteryZone.q: How did James Prinsep decipher the Brahmi script? Reconstruct the process.
masteryZone.sol: Prinsep studied multiple rock and pillar edicts, matching recurring symbols at the end of statements. He realized that a common set of characters represented the word 'danam' (gift) and linked it to the donor. Using this linguistic key, he reconstructed the Brahmi alphabet step-by-step to read the complete Prakrit statements.

masteryZone.q: How does the Sohgaura copper plate demonstrate early state administrative mechanisms?
masteryZone.sol: The Sohgaura plate lists royal orders detailing storehouses equipped with grain, fodder, and tools to be distributed during emergencies. This proves the existence of a structured famine-relief administrative policy and state grain storage infrastructure in the pre-Christian era.

masteryZone.q: An excavation of a historic layer in South India uncovers hundreds of gold coins bearing the head of Roman Emperor Augustus, alongside a few local Satavahana copper coins. Reconstruct the trade dynamics of this site.
masteryZone.sol: The presence of Roman gold coins indicates highly profitable maritime trade links with Rome. India exported luxury goods like pepper, silk, and spices and imported Roman gold and wine. The foreign coins were used as bullion for high-value transactions, while local copper coins served for daily domestic trade.

masteryZone.q: In a single field in Uttar Pradesh, a farmer uncovers a clay pot containing 500 gold coins. The coins of early layers are 98% pure gold; the coins of late layers are 70% pure gold. What socio-political process does this hoard record?
masteryZone.sol: This hoard records a period of dynastic and economic decline (debasement of currency). The transition from high purity to alloyed gold shows a fiscal crisis, likely due to war, loss of trade routes, or treasury exhaustion, leading the state to mix gold with silver or copper to sustain coin volumes.

masteryZone.q: An inscription found on a temple wall details a land grant to a Brahmin community, listing the fields, tax exemptions, and punishments for violators. Analyze its historical value.
masteryZone.sol: This inscription is a primary legal record of land tenure and feudal relations. It reveals the agricultural economy (fields), the state's fiscal structure (tax exemptions), the social hierarchy (patronage of Brahmins), and the judicial capacity of the rulers (punishments).

masteryZone.q: Explain the difference between Epigraphy and Palaeography to a student. Use a simple visual comparison.
masteryZone.sol: Think of a historic signpost: **Epigraphy** is studying *what* is written on the signpost (the message, the historical events, the ruler's name). **Palaeography** is studying *how* it is written (the shape of the letters, the script style, the slant of the handwriting, and how it evolved over centuries).

masteryZone.q: How do punch-marked coins differ from modern coins? Explain key manufacturing differences.
masteryZone.sol:
1. **Legends**: Modern coins have printed words (denominations, dates). Punch-marked coins had no text, only symbols.
2. **Shape**: Modern coins are perfectly round and uniform. Punch-marked coins were irregular sheets cut with shears.
3. **Method**: Modern coins are struck in precise hydraulic press dies. Punch-marked coins had symbols hammered onto cold metal piece-by-piece using separate punches.

masteryZone.q: Explain the historical significance of the Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I.
masteryZone.sol:
The Junagadh inscription is significant because:
1. **Language**: It is the first major long inscription written in classical, poetic Sanskrit, showing the rise of royal Sanskrit patronage.
2. **Engineering**: It records the history of the Sudarshana Lake dam, built during Chandragupta Maurya's reign and repaired by Rudradaman without taxing his subjects, showcasing early water management and state welfare policies.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Ptolemy's Geography was highly accurate in mapping the peninsular shape of India.
Reason (R): He utilized advanced GPS satellites to record the coordinates of Barygaza and Arikamedu.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. Ptolemy's map suffered from severe distortions, squeezing the peninsular shape of India, and GPS satellites did not exist.

sections.title: 3. Literary Sources (Vedic, Puranic, Buddhist & Jain)
sections.content:
Texts composed in the historic period provide oral memories, geographical references, and socio-economic clues that help reconstruct protohistory and early transitions to agriculture.

Vedic & Puranic Literature
  • Rigveda (c. 1500–1200 BCE): Oldest Indo-European text; pastoral, tribal society; lists rivers (Sapta Sindhu), providing geography of the Punjab and Indus.
  • Later Vedic Texts: Yajur, Sama, and Atharva Vedas plus Brahmanas describe expansion eastward into the Ganga valley, transition to iron, and settled farming.
  • Puranas: Contain valuable genealogies of ancient dynasties, from solar and lunar lineages to post-Mahabharata historical kings.
Buddhist & Jain Literature
  • Pali Canon (Tripitakas): Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma Pitakas provide a record of urban socio-political life in the 6th century BCE.
  • Jatakas: 547 folklore stories of Buddha's prior births; contain rich descriptions of crafts, guilds, merchant trade routes, and rural economics.
  • Jain Angas: Focus on early monastic rules and Mahavira's life teachings, recording geographical routes and early urban centers.

masteryZone.q: The oldest Indo-European literary text, which provides geographical details of the Sapta Sindhu (land of seven rivers) region, is:
masteryZone.sol: The Rigveda (c. 1500-1200 BCE) is the oldest Veda and details the pastoral Vedic tribes living in the Sapta Sindhu region.

masteryZone.q: Which category of Vedic literature explains the ritualistic meaning and execution of sacrifices?
masteryZone.sol: Brahmanas are prose texts appended to the Vedas that explain the ritualistic application, rules, and meaning of sacrifices.

masteryZone.q: The philosophical treatises of ancient India that reflect late Vedic intellectual shifts and focus on Brahman/Atman are:
masteryZone.sol: The Upanishads (c. 800-500 BCE) are philosophical works focusing on the nature of reality, soul (Atman), and absolute truth (Brahman).

masteryZone.q: In which language was the Buddhist canonical literature (Tripitakas) written?
masteryZone.sol: The Tripitakas (Sutta, Vinaya, Abhidhamma) were compiled in the Pali language, reflecting the vernacular tongue of the masses in North India.

masteryZone.q: The Jain canonical texts (Angas) were primarily written and codified in which ancient language?
masteryZone.sol: Jain canonical literature was composed in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit and codified at the Council of Valabhi in the 5th/6th century CE.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following texts belong to the Buddhist Pali Canon (Tripitakas)? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma are the three baskets (Tripitakas) of Pali Buddhism. Kalpasutra is a Jain text composed by Bhadrabahu.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Jataka stories? (Select all that apply)
opts: Depict previous births of the Buddha
Provide descriptions of guilds and trade routes
masteryZone.sol: Jatakas are written in Pali, depict prior births of the Buddha, consist of 547 tales, and offer valuable social, guild, and trade route data.

masteryZone.q: Which rivers are explicitly mentioned in the Rigvedic Nadistuti (river hymn)? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Rigvedic Nadistuti lists rivers including Sindhu, Sarasvati, Ganga, and Yamuna. Narmada is not mentioned in the early Rigveda.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are parts of the historical Puranas' five characteristics (Pancha Lakshana)? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Pancha Lakshana of Puranas are: Sarga, Pratisarga, Vamsha, Manvantara, and Vamshanucharita. Dharma is not one of the five core literary classifications.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following texts contain detailed rules of conduct for Buddhist monks? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Vinaya Pitaka and its core section, the Pratimoksha, contain code of conduct rules for monks. Sutta Pitaka lists Buddha's sermons; Angas are Jain texts.

masteryZone.q: The Rigveda is composed in classical Sanskrit, identical to the language used by Kalidasa.
masteryZone.sol: The Rigveda is written in Vedic Sanskrit, which differs significantly in grammar and vocabulary from classical Sanskrit used by Kalidasa.

masteryZone.q: Later Vedic texts describe the expansion of settled agricultural communities eastward into the Ganga valley.
masteryZone.sol: Later Vedic works like the Shatapatha Brahmana detail the clearing of forests using fire and iron axes to settle the Ganga valley.

masteryZone.q: The Upanishads reject ritualism and focus primarily on metaphysical theories of Atman and Karma.
masteryZone.sol: The Upanishads represent a major intellectual revolt against the ritual-heavy Brahmanical practices, shifting focus to spiritual self-knowledge.

masteryZone.q: The Puranas contain valuable genealogical tables of ancient historical dynasties.
masteryZone.sol: The Puranas list dynasties of the historic period (Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Maurya, Shunga, Kanva, Satavahana, Gupta) in their Vamshanucharita sections.

masteryZone.q: Jataka stories contain valuable socio-economic information regarding craft guilds and ancient trade guilds.
masteryZone.sol: Jatakas frequently mention caravan merchants (sarthavaha), routes, and specific craft guilds (seni) operating in urban centers.

masteryZone.q: The Ramayana is older than the Rigveda and describes pre-metallic Paleolithic cultures.
masteryZone.sol: The Ramayana is much younger than the Rigveda (core composed c. 500-300 BCE) and describes an advanced Iron Age urban society, not Paleolithic.

masteryZone.q: Buddhist texts were written in Prakrit to ensure Brahmin scholars could read them easily.
masteryZone.sol: Buddhist texts were written in Pali (a vernacular tongue) to bypass Sanskrit and allow ordinary people, rather than just elite Brahmins, to understand them.

masteryZone.q: The Shatapatha Brahmana describes the famous legend of Videgha Mathava carrying sacrificial fire east to the Sadaneera (Gandak) river.
masteryZone.sol: This legend symbolizes the eastward expansion of Vedic Aryan culture and agriculture from the Sarasvati region into North Bihar.

masteryZone.q: The oldest of the four Vedas, containing hymns dedicated to natural deities, is the ________.
masteryZone.sol: The Rigveda has 1,028 hymns divided into 10 Mandalas.

masteryZone.q: The prose texts appended to Vedas explaining the science and rules of sacrificial rituals are called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Each Veda has specific Brahmanas associated with it (e.g. Shatapatha Brahmana of Yajur Veda).

masteryZone.q: The philosophical ending sections of the Vedic corpus are called Upanishads or ________.
masteryZone.sol: Vedanta literally means 'the end of the Vedas', indicating both position and ultimate knowledge.

masteryZone.q: The 547 tales detailing prior lives of Gautama Buddha before his final enlightenment are the ________.
masteryZone.sol: Jatakas form a key part of the Sutta Pitaka's Khuddaka Nikaya.

masteryZone.q: The Jain canonical texts compiled at the Valabhi Council are known as the twelve ________.
masteryZone.sol: The Jain canon is based on the 12 Angas, written in Prakrit.

masteryZone.q: The famous Rigvedic geographical term 'Sapta Sindhu' refers to the Land of ________ Rivers.
masteryZone.sol: It refers to the Indus River and its five Punjab tributaries plus the Sarasvati River.

masteryZone.q: The epic Mahabharata is historically attributed to the compilation by the sage ________.
masteryZone.sol: Sage Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa is credited with compiling the Mahabharata.

masteryZone.q: The legendary river Sadaneera, mentioned in later Vedic texts as the eastern boundary of Aryan culture, is modern ________.
masteryZone.sol: Sadaneera corresponds to the modern Gandak River flowing through Bihar.

masteryZone.q: Match the Vedic texts with their literary category:
masteryZone.sol: Rigveda contains hymns; Shatapatha Brahmana details rituals; Brihadaranyaka is an Upanishad/philosophical discourse.

masteryZone.q: Match the heterodox texts with their religious tradition:
masteryZone.sol: Vinaya Pitaka is Buddhist; Acharanga Sutra is Jain; Bhagavad Gita is Hindu.

masteryZone.q: Match the ancient terms with their historical meaning:
masteryZone.sol: Sapta Sindhu is the seven rivers region, seni is a craft guild, and sarthavaha is a caravan merchant leader.

masteryZone.q: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
masteryZone.sol: Rigveda.

masteryZone.q: What language was primarily used to compose early Buddhist literature?
masteryZone.sol: Pali language.

masteryZone.q: Which text describes the legendary Aryan expansion eastward to the Sadaneera River?
masteryZone.sol: Shatapatha Brahmana.

masteryZone.q: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Upanishad'?
masteryZone.sol: To sit down near (a teacher to receive secret instruction).

masteryZone.q: Name the division of the Buddhist Pali canon that contains the moral discourses and sermons of Buddha.
masteryZone.sol: Sutta Pitaka.

masteryZone.q: In which ancient language were early Jain texts like the Angas written?
masteryZone.sol: Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

masteryZone.q: Which Sanskrit term refers to the five core characteristics of Puranas?
masteryZone.sol: Pancha Lakshana.

masteryZone.q: Explain the historical utility of the Jataka tales.
masteryZone.sol: They provide descriptions of social life, guilds, crafts, and trade routes of early historic India (c. 6th-5th century BCE).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Rigvedic society was primarily pastoral and nomadic.
Reason (R): The text contains numerous hymns honoring cows and horses, and lacks description of major brick cities or canal networks.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains the pastoral/nomadic nature of Rigvedic society based on text markers.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Later Vedic texts represent a shift toward settled agriculture in the Gangetic basin.
Reason (R): Iron tools (krishna-ayas) are mentioned in later Vedic works, facilitating the clearing of heavy soils.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains how iron enabled Gangetic agriculture and settled life.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Upanishads represent the zenith of ritual-sacrifice descriptions.
Reason (R): Upanishadic thinkers sought to establish the absolute authority of Vedic sacrificial priests.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false and R is false. Upanishads criticized ritualism, shifting the focus to internal philosophy (Atman/Brahman) and self-realization.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Pali was chosen as the medium of early Buddhist texts.
Reason (R): Buddha rejected elite Sanskrit and wanted his teachings accessible to the common masses in their local dialect.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains why Pali was used.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Puranic genealogies (Vamshanucharita) are ignored by modern historians.
Reason (R): Puranic records contain dynastic lines mixed with mythological timelines, making them completely unreliable.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false but R is true. While Puranas mix mythology, modern historians do NOT ignore them; they are carefully cross-referenced with inscriptions to reconstruct Maurya, Satavahana, and Gupta chronologies.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Jataka stories are excellent sources for reconstruction of Iron Age trade networks.
Reason (R): They contain descriptions of merchants traveling to Suvarnabhumi (Southeast Asia) and utilizing specialized guilds.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R provides the reasoning for Jatakas' value in trade studies.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Jain canonical literature (Angas) was codified during the Valabhi council.
Reason (R): The text was written in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit to prevent common masses from accessing monastic secrets.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true but R is false. Prakrit was chosen specifically because it was a vernacular language of the common people, not to hide secrets.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Epics like Ramayana and Mahabharata are used carefully as historical records.
Reason (R): They underwent multiple revisions and expansions over centuries, introducing younger Iron Age features into older narratives.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true, and R explains why historians exercise caution when using epics for dating.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Rigvedic literature:
1. It contains 1,028 hymns organized into 10 Mandalas.
2. The Nadistuti hymn honors the Indus (Sindhu) river as the most prominent river.
3. The tenth Mandala contains the Purusha Sukta, which introduces the four Varnas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: All three statements are correct and define key historical data extracted from the Rigvedic Samhita.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Buddhist canon:
1. The Vinaya Pitaka deals with rules of discipline for monks.
2. The Sutta Pitaka contains the philosophical analysis of Buddhist psychology.
3. The Abhidhamma Pitaka contains the moral sermons of the Buddha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Only statement 1 is correct. Sutta Pitaka contains sermons; Abhidhamma Pitaka contains the philosophical and psychological analysis.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to Jain canonical literature, which of the following statements are correct?
1. It was codified at the Valabhi Council in Gujarat.
2. The texts are written in Sanskrit, the language of royal courts.
3. The Acharanga Sutra details the rules of conduct for Jain monks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Jain canon was composed in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

masteryZone.q:
Regarding later Vedic geography, consider the following statements:
1. Shatapatha Brahmana describes the myth of Videgha Mathava clearing forests with fire.
2. Later Vedic literature indicates the center of Aryan culture shifted from Indus to Ganga-Yamuna Doab.
3. The river Sarasvati is praised as the ultimate boundary in later Vedic texts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. In later Vedic times, Sarasvati was drying up and Ganga-Yamuna became the core area, with Sadaneera (Gandak) as the eastern limit.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Puranas as historical sources:
1. The genealogies of kings are preserved in the Vamshanucharita section.
2. Puranas list historical dynasties like Nandas and Mauryas in future tense format.
3. The Vishnu Purana provides crucial information regarding the Satavahana dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vishnu Purana details Mauryan dynasty; Matsya Purana details Satavahanas.

masteryZone.q: Why does later Vedic literature show a major transition in agricultural techniques compared to early Rigvedic hymns?
masteryZone.sol: Rigvedic society was pastoralist, utilizing light wooden plows (langala). In the later Vedic period, Aryans expanded into the Gangetic valley where they encountered hard alluvial clay. They adapted by utilizing heavy iron-shod plows and iron axes (krishna-ayas) to clear dense monsoon forests, shifting to intensive rice cultivation.

masteryZone.q: Why are Upanishads considered a philosophical reaction against Brahmanas?
masteryZone.sol: Brahmanas focused heavily on the mechanics, costs, and execution of animal sacrifices and priest-led rituals. Upanishads represented a spiritual reaction, declaring rituals to be 'frail boats' and shifting focus to philosophical questions of self-realization, absolute truth (Brahman), and the inner soul (Atman).

masteryZone.q: Why do Buddhist Jataka stories represent reliable sources for early historic trade geography?
masteryZone.sol: Although Jatakas are moral fables, they reflect the contemporary world of the compilers. They describe caravan traders (sarthavaha) traveling along specific highways (Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha), naming rivers, ports, and cities, providing historians with realistic geographic maps of trade networks.

masteryZone.q: How does the myth of Videgha Mathava in Shatapatha Brahmana explain historical geography?
masteryZone.sol: The myth describes Videgha Mathava carrying Agni (sacrificial fire) eastward from the Sarasvati, burning forests along the way, until reaching the Sadaneera River (modern Gandak). This explains the historical process of Aryan migration, clearing Gangetic forests using fire, and establishing agriculture in Bihar.

masteryZone.q: How did the compilation of Jain Angas at Valabhi shape early medieval Western Indian history?
masteryZone.sol: By compiling and writing down oral traditions at Valabhi (Gujarat, c. 5th-6th cent. CE), Jain scholars preserved rules, geography, and genealogies. This codified canon stimulated Jain temple networks, mercantile writing, and Prakrit literature in Western India, linking merchant wealth to Jain institutions.

masteryZone.q: How do Puranas help reconstruct dynastic chronologies when epigraphic evidence is missing?
masteryZone.sol: Puranas record dynastic lists, listing the number of kings in a dynasty and their total reign years (e.g. Satavahanas or Mauryas). Historians cross-reference these lists with sporadic coins and foreign accounts to build structural timelines for periods lacking extensive royal inscriptions.

masteryZone.q: A researcher attempts to date a text describing a rich capital city with brick gates, stone towers, and gold coins. The text is claimed to be Rigvedic. Analyze this claim.
masteryZone.sol: The claim is historically invalid. Rigvedic society (c. 1500–1200 BCE) was a pastoral, non-urban culture that did not construct brick cities or stone fortifications. Gold currency (coins) did not exist in India until the Indo-Greek/Kushan period. The text must belong to a late historical period (c. 4th century BCE or later).

masteryZone.q: An economist studies ancient Indian interest rates and guild rules. Which literary sources (Buddhist, Jain, Brahmanical) should they select, and why?
masteryZone.sol:
They should select: 1. Dharmasutras/Manusmriti (Brahmanical) for legal limits on interest rates.
2. Jatakas (Buddhist) for realistic case studies of merchant credit, caravan financing, and guild disputes.
3. Angas (Jain) for merchant routes, proving how different traditions recorded economic laws and practices.

masteryZone.q: During excavation of a site in Bihar, archaeologists find iron tools associated with charred rice grains in a layer dated to c. 800 BCE. Which later Vedic literary texts corroborate this archaeological phase?
masteryZone.sol: This archaeological phase is corroborated by later Vedic texts, particularly the Shatapatha Brahmana (which details the expansion into Bihar/Sadaneera and iron tool use) and the Atharvaveda (which mentions iron plowshares, indicating settled rice farming in the Ganga valley).

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Sruthi' versus 'Smriti' in ancient Indian literature to a student. Use a modern legal analogy.
masteryZone.sol:
1. **Shruti** (Hearing): Believed to be direct cosmic truth heard by sages. It is eternal and unchangeable. Analogy: The Constitution (supreme, permanent law).
2. **Smriti** (Memory): Human recollections and compilations of traditions. They adapt to changing social eras. Analogy: Bylaws or amendments (created by humans, open to revision).

masteryZone.q: How would you teach a student the historical value of the Puranas? Outline three warning traps.
masteryZone.sol:
1. **Pancha Lakshana**: Teach that Puranas contain genealogies (Vamsha) essential for timelines.
2. **Trap 1 (Future Tense)**: Explain that dynastic histories are written in a 'prophecy' format, but record past facts.
3. **Trap 2 (Mythology)**: Warn that gods and sages are mixed with human kings; mythological years must be filtered out.
4. **Trap 3 (Varying Editions)**: Emphasize that different Puranas must be cross-checked, as they contain sectarian biases.

masteryZone.q: Explain why the transition from Sanskrit in Vedas to Pali in Buddhism was a socio-political revolution.
masteryZone.sol: Sanskrit was the language of the elite Brahmins, who claimed exclusive rights to read and execute Vedic rituals, creating a social monopoly. By preaching and writing in Pali, the language of ordinary merchants, farmers, and women, Buddhism demystified spiritual knowledge, bypassing Brahmin authority and creating a democratic literary culture.

sections.title: 4. Foreign Accounts & Travellers
sections.content:
Descriptions left by foreign visitors offer an external, objective perspective on Indian society, trade, and politics, serving as chronological anchors for dating local history.

Greek & Roman Accounts
  • Megasthenes (c. 300 BCE): Wrote Indica, serving as Chandragupta Maurya's ambassador. Describes Maurya administrative system, Pataliputra, and the 7-caste division.
  • Periplus of the Erythraean Sea: Anonymous 1st-century CE sailor's log; documents Indian ports (Barygaza, Muziris, Arikamedu) and trade with Rome.
  • Pliny & Ptolemy: Pliny (1st cent. CE) lamented Rome's trade drain to India; Ptolemy (2nd cent. CE) created a geographic map detailing Indian rivers and ports.
Chinese & Persian Travellers
  • Fa-Hien (399–414 CE): Visited during Gupta rule (Chandragupta II); focused on Buddhist monasticism and social peace in North India.
  • Hiuen Tsang (630–645 CE): Visited during Harsha's reign; studied at Nalanda; recorded details of assembly at Kanauj and Indian social classes.
  • Al-Biruni (11th Century CE): Accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni; wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, a deep academic study of Indian sciences, mathematics, and philosophy.

masteryZone.q: Which Greek ambassador visited the Mauryan court of Chandragupta Maurya and wrote the famous text 'Indica'?
masteryZone.sol: Megasthenes served as the Seleucid ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya's court and compiled 'Indica', which survives only in fragments.

masteryZone.q: Which Roman writer wrote the 'Naturalis Historia' (Natural History) in Latin and lamented the drain of Roman gold to India?
masteryZone.sol: Pliny the Elder wrote Natural History in Latin (1st century CE), noting that Rome drained 55 million sesterces annually to India for luxury goods.

masteryZone.q: The anonymous 1st-century CE sailor's guidebook that provides detailed descriptions of ports, trade routes, and exports along the Indian Ocean is:
masteryZone.sol: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea is an anonymous Greek logbook documenting Indian ports like Barygaza (Bharuch), Muziris, and Arikamedu.

masteryZone.q: Which Chinese Buddhist pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Gupta dynasty) and wrote 'Fo-Kwo-Ki'?
masteryZone.sol: Fa-Hien (399-414 CE) visited India during the Gupta reign of Chandragupta II to collect Buddhist scriptures.

masteryZone.q: The 11th-century Central Asian polymath who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' was:
masteryZone.sol: Al-Biruni wrote Tarikh-al-Hind (Kitab-ul-Hind) in Arabic, providing an objective study of Indian culture, astronomy, mathematics, and caste system.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Chinese travellers visited India during the post-Gupta/Harsha and early medieval periods? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Hiuen Tsang (7th century, Harsha) and I-Tsing (late 7th century) visited in the post-Gupta era. Fa-Hien visited in the Gupta era. Megasthenes was Greek.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Indian ports are explicitly documented in the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Barygaza, Muziris, and Poduke (Arikamedu) are ports documented in the Periplus. Pataliputra is an inland capital city.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following descriptions represent Megasthenes' observations in 'Indica'? (Select all that apply)
opts: Divided Indian society into seven castes
Stated that slavery was absent in India
Described the administrative board of Pataliputra
Recorded the rise of Buddhism under Ashoka
masteryZone.sol: Megasthenes described 7 castes, noted no slavery, and detailed Pataliputra administration. Ashoka reigned after Megasthenes' visit.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following fields of study did Al-Biruni analyze in 'Kitab-ul-Hind'? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Al-Biruni studied Sanskrit, Hindu philosophy, astronomy, and math. He did not analyze Chola genealogies, as he was based in northwestern India.

masteryZone.q: Which Roman or Greek writers cite fragments of Megasthenes' lost 'Indica' in their own works? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Arrian, Strabo, Diodorus, and Pliny cite Megasthenes' Indica. Al-Biruni was an 11th-century Arabic-writing Persian scholar.

masteryZone.q: Herodotus, the 'Father of History', visited the Gangetic plains and described the Mauryan administration.
masteryZone.sol: Herodotus never visited India; he wrote about the Persian Satrapy of Gandhara based on secondary Persian accounts.

masteryZone.q: Megasthenes' original manuscript of 'Indica' is preserved in the British Museum.
masteryZone.sol: Megasthenes' original 'Indica' is completely lost. Its contents are known only through citations in later Greek and Roman texts.

masteryZone.q: The anonymous work 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' was written by a Roman emperor.
masteryZone.sol: It was written by an anonymous Greek-speaking merchant-sailor based in Alexandria, Egypt, not an emperor.

masteryZone.q: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of Harsha and studied at Nalanda University.
masteryZone.sol: Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda during Harsha's reign. Fa-Hien visited during the Gupta period (Chandragupta II) when Nalanda was not yet a major center.

masteryZone.q: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) attended the great religious assembly at Kanauj organized by King Harsha.
masteryZone.sol: Hiuen Tsang was the guest of honor at Harsha's Kanauj assembly in 643 CE.

masteryZone.q: Al-Biruni translated Sanskrit works, including Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, into Arabic.
masteryZone.sol: Al-Biruni translated Sanskrit mathematical, astronomical, and philosophical texts (like Yoga Sutras) into Arabic.

masteryZone.q: Ptolemy's Geography (2nd century CE) contains the first detailed map of India with river courses.
masteryZone.sol: Ptolemy mapped India's rivers and ports, which, despite structural distortions, served as primary cartographic data.

masteryZone.q: Fa-Hien described the Gupta administration as extremely harsh, with frequent executions and heavy taxes.
masteryZone.sol: Fa-Hien described Gupta administration as mild, noting that capital punishment was rare, travel was safe, and taxes were light.

masteryZone.q: The Seleucid ambassador who wrote 'Indica' was ________.
masteryZone.sol: Megasthenes stayed in Pataliputra as the envoy of Seleucus I Nicator.

masteryZone.q: The 1st-century CE Roman author who lamented the drainage of Roman gold to India in 'Natural History' was ________.
masteryZone.sol: Pliny lamented the economic drain caused by Rome's import of Indian luxuries.

masteryZone.q: The anonymous Greek guidebook describing Indian ports and Ocean trade routes is the ________.
masteryZone.sol: Written in Greek by an Egyptian Greek sailor in the 1st century CE.

masteryZone.q: The Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the reign of King Harsha was ________.
masteryZone.sol: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) traveled to India between 630 and 645 CE.

masteryZone.q: Al-Biruni's famous Arabic treatise on Indian sciences, customs, and philosophy is titled ________.
masteryZone.sol: Also known as Tarikh-al-Hind or Tahqiq-ma-lil-Hind.

masteryZone.q: The Greek writer known as the 'Father of History' who first mentioned 'Indica' was ________.
masteryZone.sol: Herodotus wrote about the Persian-Indian borderlands in the 5th century BCE.

masteryZone.q: The 2nd-century CE geographer who drew a famous map locating Indian rivers and ports was ________.
masteryZone.sol: Claudius Ptolemy wrote the 'Geographia' in Alexandria.

masteryZone.q: The 7th-century CE Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who recorded Nalanda's monastic rules after Xuanzang was ________.
masteryZone.sol: I-Tsing (Yijing) stayed at Nalanda for ten years translating texts.

masteryZone.q: Match the travellers with their country of origin:
masteryZone.sol: Megasthenes is Greek; Fa-Hien is Chinese; Al-Biruni is Persian/Khwarazmian.

masteryZone.q: Match the foreign accounts with their primary language:
